The test image shows two tomatoes (fruit/pod) with large, circular, sunken, dark lesions. The right tomato clearly shows concentric rings with a dark center and pinkish-tan border. The left tomato is more advanced with dark/black sporulation masses. This pattern strongly suggests Anthracnose.

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms the pattern of dark, sunken, spreading lesions on fruit that is characteristic of Anthracnose.

**Analysis summary:**
- **Affected part**: Fruit/pod (tomatoes)
- **Key features in test image**: Circular, sunken, dark lesions with clear concentric rings (especially visible on right tomato), dark fungal structures in the center, pinkish-tan border zone, progressive darkening from center outward
- **Best match**: Anthracnose - "initially appears as small, circular, water-soaked and sunken spots on overripe tomatoes. These lesions form concentric rings, expand to ½" in diameter, darken progressively" and "concentric ring pattern with tan center and dark specks; water-soaked and sunken lesions"
- The left tomato shows an advanced/merged lesion with dark sporulation masses (salmon-colored spores appear dark when dried)
